pairs.locus: William of Apulia, Gesta Roberti Wiscardi 1.461-469
pairs.question: Pretii cum nulla facultas sit mihi, quo possim populum donare potentem, cur populus vester me vult sibi praefore, miror. Vos etenim novi diversis rebus egere; quas cum non dedero, me non dare posse dolebo.
pairs.answer: Nostrum te principe nullus pauper erit vel egens, duce te fortuna favebit, consiliique vias, duce quas genitore solebat pandere, te nobis effecto principe pandet.
pairs.derivation: Argirous' entire speech to the leading men of Bari is one extended question/wonder containing the real interrogative 'cur populus vester me vult sibi praefore' (why does your people want me to rule them, given I have no wealth to give). Dropped the framing tag 'Taliter affatur:' before it; capitalized 'Pretii'. The people's reply (introduced by the dropped framing 'Illi respondent:') genuinely answers the 'cur' by giving the reason: under his rule none will be poor and he will open the paths of counsel as his father did. The reply is short and wholly answering, kept entire to the first full stop ('pandet.'); what follows ('Hoc ubi dixerunt, sublimant protinus illum...') is narration of their acclaiming him, omitted.
